Academic career at UTM

Joined the Faculty of Computing as a lecturer in 2006, building a career that spans teaching, research, postgraduate supervision and institutional leadership.

04 — Research and scholarship

Research themes

Pervasive and connected computing

Intelligent environments, IoT and context-aware systems.

Wireless sensor networks

Resilient sensing, routing and deployment.

Underwater acoustic networks

Communication and networking in difficult underwater environments.

Motion planning

Robot navigation, path planning and bio-inspired optimisation.

Indoor positioning

WiFi, camera-based localisation and hybrid positioning.

AI for built heritage

Sensing and predictive analysis for heritage buildings, with links to UTM KALAM.

05 — Postgraduate supervision

Developing researchers

Twenty-one PhD candidates and sixteen Master’s candidates have completed their degrees under my supervision. My programme role also includes supporting the wider PhD in Computer Science community at UTM.

06 — Teaching, grants and service

Academic contribution

Teaching

Postgraduate and undergraduate

Eight undergraduate subjects across twenty-eight semesters and 702+ students since 2006. Postgraduate teaching includes Research Methodology in Computer Science, Advanced Computer Systems and Architecture, and Advanced Computer Networks and Cloud Computing. Full teaching record →

Research projects

Principal investigator and team member

Roles across government, university and industry-supported projects, including IoT heritage monitoring, smart infrastructure, network security and community applications.
